articles.title: Duleep Trophy Final: East Zone finish day 1 on 385/4 as Ishan Kishan remains unbeaten on 111
articles.summary: Cricket News: Ishan Kishan led from the front with a superb unbeaten century as East Zone finished Day 1 of the Duleep Trophy 2026 final on 385/4 against South Zone.
articles.body: Ishan Kishan led from the front with a superb unbeaten century as East Zone finished Day 1 of the Duleep Trophy 2026 final on 385/4 against South Zone at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai on Sunday.After winning the toss and opting to bat, Kishan anchored a strong batting display from East Zone, scoring 111 not out off 135 balls. His innings featured 14 fours and two sixes as he took control of the contest in the final session.Kishan found an excellent partner in Kumar Kushagra, who remained unbeaten on 63 off 75 balls. The pair added an unbeaten 144-run partnership for the fifth wicket off 160 balls, completely taking the game away from South Zone towards the end of the day.Kishan takes charge after Mohan fallsEast Zone made a solid start through Abhimanyu Easwaran (72) and teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (44). Easwaran and Sooryavanshi gave the side a strong platform before both departed. Sudip Kumar Gharami was then dismissed for 6, bringing Shikhar Mohan to the crease. Mohan played a composed knock of 85 off 120 balls, helping East Zone build another important partnership before Chama Milind ended his innings at 241/4.That dismissal brought Kishan and Kushagra together, and the pair ensured there were no further setbacks.Kishan accelerated as the innings progressed and brought up his century in style, remaining unbeaten at the close. His knock was particularly important given his role as captain, with East Zone now firmly in control after the opening day.South Zone struggle for breakthroughsSouth Zone's bowling attack found little assistance from a placid batting surface, while the bowlers also struggled with consistency. Chama Milind was the most successful bowler, finishing the day with figures of 2/56 from 13 overs. Tripurana Vijay picked up one wicket but conceded 114 runs from his 22 overs.Mohammed Siraj, meanwhile, went wicketless despite bowling 14 overs and conceded 96 runs. East Zone also benefited from a late surge, scoring 74 runs without losing a wicket in the final 10 overs. Kishan and Kushagra's partnership allowed them to finish the day strongly at 385/4.With Kishan unbeaten on 111 and Kushagra on 63, East Zone will resume on Day 2 with an opportunity to push towards a total of 400 and beyond. South Zone, meanwhile, will desperately need early wickets with the second new ball to prevent East Zone from building an even bigger first-innings total.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Title-chasing Nottinghamshire lose Kyle Verreynne ahead of crucial County Championship run-in
articles.summary: Cricket News: Nottinghamshire’s County Championship title push has suffered a blow after South Africa wicketkeeper-batter Kyle Verreynne was recalled early by Crick.
articles.body: Nottinghamshire’s County Championship title push has suffered a blow after South Africa wicketkeeper-batter Kyle Verreynne was recalled early by Cricket South Africa, ruling him out of the club’s final three matches of the season.Verreynne, 29, is in his third stint with Nottinghamshire and had initially agreed to play in all of the club’s red-ball fixtures this summer. However, his central contract commitments with South Africa take priority as the Proteas prepare for a three-Test home series against Australia.His final appearance for Nottinghamshire this season will come against Leicestershire at Trent Bridge, before he returns to South Africa.Verreynne departure comes at crucial stageVerreynne’s departure comes at a crucial stage of Nottinghamshire’s campaign. They currently sit second in the County Championship, four points behind leaders Somerset and one point ahead of third-placed Warwickshire, with just three rounds remaining.The club will now have to manage the final stretch of the title race without their first-choice wicketkeeper, with fixtures against Hampshire, Sussex and Yorkshire still to come.Despite his early departure, Verreynne said he would continue to follow Nottinghamshire’s title challenge closely.“I think I've said it so many times, the club's got a really special place. It's got a special place to me, so I'll be watching closely.”He added:“The team's in a good position at the moment, playing some really good cricket. I think it's going to be quite an exciting run-in, so I'll be keeping a close eye.”Mick Newell acknowledges CSA’s decisionNottinghamshire Director of Cricket Mick Newell admitted that losing Verreynne at this point of the season was far from ideal, although the club understood South Africa’s position.“It’s not ideal that we’re losing Kyle at this point in the season, but we understand the decision made by Cricket South Africa, and he returns with our best wishes for a busy winter.”Newell also praised Verreynne’s contribution during his latest spell with the club, saying his performances had helped Nottinghamshire put themselves in a strong position heading into the final weeks of the Championship.“We’ve been very happy to have Kyle with us for most of the summer, during which his contributions have put us in a strong position as we head towards the final few matches,” he said.With several South African players being recalled from county cricket ahead of the Australia series, Nottinghamshire will now look for a replacement for Verreynne.“There’s always a lot of hard work being done behind the scenes to make sure we’re prepared for every outcome, and we hope to confirm a replacement for Kyle as soon as we’re able to,” Newell added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England clinch ODI series sweep of Ireland as Sophia Dunkley hits second international century in 114-run win
articles.summary: England collapse from 260-4 to 291 all out after Sophia Dunkley (119 off 119 balls) hits run-a-ball century, but Ireland fail to threaten in run-chase; Lauren Filer (3-27), Mady Villiers (3-33) and Tilly Corteen-Coleman (2-34) impress as tourists are skittled for 177
articles.body:
Sophia Dunkley (119 off 119 balls) struck a run-a-ball century - her second in ODI cricket - as England set Ireland 292 to win, having been inserted by the visitors.

But Ireland never truly threatened in reply, despite a handful of starts for their top-order batters, as they were ultimately bowled out for 177 after 44.2 overs.

England were also bowled out short of their allotted 50 overs, as the hosts collapsed from 183-1 in the 31st over and 260-4 in the 43rd to 291 all out after 48.5.

It wouldn't prove costly, however, as Lauren Filer (3-27), Mady Villiers (3-33) and Tilly Corteen-Coleman (2-34) starred with the ball to skittle Ireland and secure a series whitewash.

Dunkley continued her fine form with the bat this summer as she cracked 15 boundaries in her sublime knock, sharing in a 73-run opening partnership with Maia Bouchier and dominating a second-wicket century stand with Jodi Grewcock (35).

It laid the foundation for what looked set to be a sizeable score of around 350 or beyond, only for things to fall apart at the back end.

Alice Capsey (10) was run out cheaply, before Dunkley holed out in the deep, and though Dani Gibson (41 off 37) and Freya Kemp (23 off 21) cracked a few lusty blows in a 46-run partnership for the fifth wicket, England lost 6-31 in the space of little more than six overs thereafter.

Ireland captain Gaby Lewis claimed a terrific catch on the long-off boundary to see the back of Kemp and trigger the collapse, with leg-spinner Cara Murray (4-56) claiming a career-first four-for.

Filer (16) dismissed Lewis early on in the Ireland reply, before Alice Tector (29) and Amy Hunter (39) laid the foundations with a 56-run second-wicket stand - but too slowly.

The tourists began to fall behind the required rate, and there was only to be one winner when the wickets began to tumble.

Corteen-Coleman first bowled Tector, Capsey then claimed a couple of stumpings - Hunter and Rebecca Stokell (14) - to continue her successful wicketkeeping audition in this series, before Orla Prendergast (24) was caught at deep midwicket.

Corteen-Coleman then cleaned up another batter, Louise Little (14), as Ireland lost their last five wickets for 10 runs in under four overs - Filer finishing off the job by dismantling Kia McCartney's stumps.

Player of the series and match Sophia Dunkley:

"It was just great to get the series win today.

"It was definitely tricky at the start. The longer you batted the easier it got. It was nice to get through that period and see us home.

"For me, it is just about staying really present. I love batting for whatever team I am playing for and it is great to be at the top of the order again in ODI cricket.

"It is definitely my goal to be at the top of the order in all formats."

"We all know she can get off to fast and furious starts. The main goal for her this series will have been match-winning contributions.

"She wanted big runs and she has done that today."

First ODI (Leicester) - England win by six wickets

Second ODI (Derby) - England win by six wickets

Third ODI (Worcester) - England win by 114 runs

articles.title: England v Ireland: Sophia Dunkley cetury seals hosts' dominant series clean sweep
articles.summary: Sophia Dunkley hits 119 as England end their international summer with a 114-run thrashing of Ireland at Worcester.
articles.body:
England 291 (48.5 overs): Dunkley 119 (119); Murray 4-56

Ireland 177 (44.2 overs): Hunter 39 (58); Filer 3-27

Sophia Dunkley's sparkling century led England to a comprehensive 114-run win in the third and final one-day international against Ireland at Worcester.

Dunkley's run-a-ball 119 set up England's 291 before Ireland were bowled out for 177 in 44.2 overs, sealing a 3-0 clean sweep for Charlie Dean's side.

England were eyeing a record total after opener Dunkley's second international century, but the innings fell away from 260-4 and they frustratingly lost their last six wickets for just 31 runs to be dismissed with seven balls unused.

Dunkley added 73 for the first wicket with Maia Bouchier, who continued her fine run of form with 39, before Jodi Grewcock also wasted a good start as she was caught and bowled for 35 and Alice Capsey was unlucky to be run out backing up for 10.

All-rounders Freya Kemp and Dani Gibson threatened to push England beyond 300 but it was the former's wicket that kickstarted the collapse as she was caught at long-on for 23 and a run of single-figure scores followed, though Gibson kicked on to an ODI-best 41.

Leg-spinner Cara Murray was the pick of Ireland's bowlers with 4-56 as the visitors fought back admirably, and England only managed to hit seven boundaries after Dunkley's departure in the 36th over.

Despite the disappointing end to the innings, England still had plenty on the board in another non-contest between bat and ball.

Amy Hunter top-scored with 39 but no Irish batter was able to score at a strike-rate above 100 and the run-rate spiralled beyond their grasp, as Mady Villiers and Lauren Filer took three wickets apiece.

The final match of the series concludes England's international summer. Their next confirmed games will come at the Champions Trophy in February, though a multi-format series against West Indies in the autumn and three ODIs against Sri Lanka are in the schedule, but the dates have not been released.

Ireland women in England 2026 Published 1 hour ago

This has been a series with an unusual context for England.

Key stars such as Lauren Bell, Sophie Ecclestone and Nat Sciver-Brunt have been rested, which has presented opportunities to experiment with the likes of fringe players in Grewcock and Tilly Corteen-Coleman.

But the curious cricketing calendar means they have few opportunities to play the format, with the autumn schedule still unconfirmed and their next home ODI coming in the Ashes next summer, meaning they have been simultaneously seeking stability.

The opening partnership was one question that needed answering after Tammy Beaumont's retirement earlier this year, and a century apiece for Dunkley and Bouchier in this series has seen them take their chance.

Of course, Ireland's bowling attack is incomparable to Australia's and to cite this as Ashes preparation would be very unrealistic, but England can only play the schedule they are given.

Dunkley had been threatening in the first two games, falling for 73 at Leicester before she was stitched up by Bouchier's poor running at Derby - but she was not to be denied a third time.

The 28-year-old started patiently, reaching her half-century off 63 balls after Bouchier dominated the strike early on, before kicking on and whacking her next fifty off just 37.

A notable change to her game has been her improvement through the off-side, scoring her runs almost equally split across both sides of the wicket - a big change for a player previously known for her leg-side dominance.

Ireland tested her with the short ball and forced her to hit to the sweepers, which she handled efficiently before her eventual downfall as she was brilliantly caught by Prendergast at deep square leg.

Sciver-Brunt is likely to slot straight back in at number three, and England have a decision to make about whether Capsey keeps the gloves over Amy Jones, but for now, Dunkley and Bouchier have solved one of coach Charlotte Edwards' headaches.

The series was also a valuable opportunity for England's crop of seamers to test themselves without Bell leading the attack, another area of their squad that needed strengthening.

With spinners dominating the T20 World Cup earlier this summer, the likes of Filer and Issy Wong were sidelined, but both have stepped up admirably.

Wong starred in the second ODI with her first international five-wicket haul before resting for this final game where Filer troubled the Irish batters throughout with her lively pace, which helped her take 3-27.

Contrastingly, Ryana Macdonald-Gay offered a change of tempo with her niggly medium-pace and Edwards will be hoping for Kemp to return to bowling fitness soon in order to give herself another option in the middle overs alongside Gibson.

Villiers took 3-33 with her off-spin as she claimed the big wickets of Hunter and Orla Prendergast, and with Corteen-Coleman waiting in Ecclestone's wings, England's bowling stocks are in a healthy position.

Ireland barely threatened to reach their target, with captain Gaby Lewis falling early for 16 to dent their hopes almost immediately and fellow opener Alice Tector trudged to 29 off 59 balls, which saw the run-rate climb steadily.

England were made to work hard for their wickets throughout a stalling middle-over phase but eventually they ripped through the lower order with Ireland's last five wickets falling in a heap for just 10 runs.

articles.title: 'Bhaiya gave me a lot of advice': Shikhar Mohan’s 85 gives East Zone a lift; Reveals Ishan Kishan’s guidance
articles.summary: Cricket News: Shikhar Mohan, Jharkhand batter credited captain Ishan Kishan’s constant guidance after making an impressive 85 on his Duleep Trophy debut against Sou.
articles.body: Shikhar Mohan, Jharkhand batter credited captain Ishan Kishan’s constant guidance after making an impressive 85 on his Duleep Trophy debut against South Zone in the 2026/27 final.Mohan, who came into the East Zone XI as a replacement for Jharkhand teammate Virat Singh, played a key role in rebuilding the innings after the early wickets. He added 94 runs for the third wicket with Kishan, helping East Zone recover and take control on the opening day.Kishan remained unbeaten on 111 at stumps, while Kumar Kushagra was not out on 63 as East Zone finished the day on 385/4 in 79 overs.“Ishan bhaiya was giving me a lot of advice while batting. He was telling me what shot is on and what is not. Thanks to that, we had a great partnership,” Mohan told reporters after play.Ranji form and T20 experience boost debutMohan earned his place in the East Zone side after an outstanding debut Ranji Trophy season, where he scored 613 runs at an average of 55.72. Although primarily an opener, he had no issues adapting to the No. 3 position with Abhimanyu Easwaran and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opening for East Zone.“My journey has been very good so far. My first season in Ranji Trophy went very well, so coming into this match, I just wanted to carry that forward. I was looking to maintain that form from the Ranji Trophy,” he said.Mohan also accepted the challenge of facing South Zone’s short-ball strategy, with five fielders stationed on the leg side. He showed patience before eventually falling to Chama Milind after an inside edge off a bouncer.“The plan was that I would leave the ball first, and when they get tired, they will give me chances to score runs. I made a poor decision and got out,” he admitted.The youngster also felt his experience in the Jharkhand T20 League helped him handle the pressure of playing in front of a sizeable crowd at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.“I think it helped a lot. The crowds there were also very good, so today when there was a big crowd, it felt normal to me,” Mohan said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Shubman Gill loses his wicket to CSK's intern bowler in his first match of Sher-e-Punjab T20 league
articles.summary: While fans expected Arshdeep Singh to be Shubman Gill's arch-nemesis in the Sher-e-Punjab Trophy, instead it is a CSK intern bowler who took his wicket.
articles.body:
Shubman Gill was dismissed for 40 by Kartik Chadha in his first Sher-e-Punjab T20 match.

Chadha served as Chennai Super Kings' intern bowler during the IPL 2025 season.

The India skipper struck seven fours and a six in a quickfire 21-ball knock for the Fazilka Falcons.

Kartik Chadha surprises Shubman Gill as he dismisses the India skipper in Sher-e-Punjab T20

Shubman Gill finally took the field for Fazilka Falcons in the Sher-e-Punjab T20 League on Saturday, and his first outing as captain produced fireworks with the bat before ending at the hands of one of CSK's own. Kartik Chadha, who spent IPL 2025 as CSK's intern bowler, dismissed the India captain for a blistering 40 off 21 balls.

Gill had been absent for the Falcons' first four matches of the tournament, with the side losing three of them as he attended the BCCI's performance review meeting in Mumbai. His arrival was the most anticipated moment of the league's season so far.

The India skipper wasted no time finding his rhythm, opening the innings and striking seven fours and a six before Chadha's leg-spin ended his cameo. The Falcons were eventually set a target they could not overcome.

Who is Kartik Chadha, the CSK intern who dismissed Shubman Gill?

Chadha is a 21-year-old right-arm leg-spinner and left-handed middle-order batter from Jalandhar, a product of CT Public School who has quietly built an impressive résumé through Punjab's age-group system.

His numbers across domestic youth cricket are striking. During the 2021-22 Under-19 Punjab tournament, Chadha emerged as the highest wicket-taker with 36 wickets in nine matches for Jalandhar district. He represented Punjab in the BCCI's Vijay Merchant Trophy and later topped the Senior One-Day Inter-District Tournament with 16 wickets in six matches.

Those performances caught the attention of Chennai Super Kings, who brought him on board as an intern bowler for the 2025 IPL season. The role gave Chadha access to the franchise's training infrastructure and coaching staff, including the chance to bowl at some of the finest batters in the competition during net sessions.

Dismissing India's Test and ODI captain in a state-level T20 is the most visible return on that investment so far, and it will not have gone unnoticed by the CSK management heading into the IPL 2027 auction cycle.

articles.title: Jordan Hermann, bowlers shine as South Africa beat Zimbabwe to clinch tri-series title
articles.summary: Batting first, South Africa posted 205/5 in 20 overs after choosing to bat. Jordan Hermann led the way with a quick half-century, while Dewald Brevis and Rub...
articles.body:
South Africa produced a strong all-round performance to beat Zimbabwe by 48 runs in the final and win the T20I tri-series at the Namibia Cricket Ground on Sunday. Batting first, South Africa posted 205/5 in 20 overs after choosing to bat. Jordan Hermann led the way with a quick half-century, while Dewald Brevis and Rubin Hermann also made important contributions. Zimbabwe struggled from the start in the chase and were bowled out for 157 in 18 overs.

Hermann gives South Africa a flying start

South Africa were without opener Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who missed the final with a niggle. But his absence did not affect the team's start. Jordan Hermann attacked the Zimbabwe bowlers from the beginning and reached his fifty in just 24 balls. His innings included eight fours and a six. He added 84 runs for the opening wicket with Connor Esterhuizen, who scored 32. Brevis then kept the pressure on Zimbabwe in the middle overs. He scored 32 from 23 balls, hitting two fours and two sixes. Rubin Hermann added 27 off 16 balls, with three fours and a six. His partnership with Brevis helped South Africa cross the 200-run mark. Brad Evans and Newman Nyamhuri took two wickets each for Zimbabwe, but South Africa finished with a big total of 205/5.

Zimbabwe needed 206 runs to win but suffered a terrible start. Ben Curran was dismissed for a first-ball duck by Eathan Bosch. Duan Jansen and Bosch then continued to trouble the Zimbabwe batters as four wickets fell inside the powerplay. Captain Sikandar Raza got a second chance when a caught-behind decision against him was overturned because Bosch had bowled a no-ball. However, South Africa captain Bjorn Fortuin soon ended Raza's stay at the crease. He finished with three wickets for 24 runs as Zimbabwe's chase fell apart.

Evans fights back but Zimbabwe fall short

Brad Evans gave Zimbabwe some hope late in the innings. The pacer scored his maiden T20I half-century and put on 52 runs for the ninth wicket with Kundai Matigimu. But Kwena Maphaka broke the partnership, and Zimbabwe were eventually bowled out in the 18th over. Duan Jansen was South Africa's best bowler, finishing with 3/38, while Bosch took 2/22. It was South Africa's third win over Zimbabwe in just eight days.

Important preparation for 2027 World Cup

The tri-series was an important preparation tournament for South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, who will co-host the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup. South Africa will now play a three-match ODI series against Namibia. Fortuin will continue to lead the team in the series.

articles.title: 'They're clearly hoping to kill him in there': Imran Khan's sons raise serious concerns
articles.summary: Cricket News: The sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan have strongly criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after th.
articles.body: The sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan have strongly criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the board was accused of threatening to abandon the Lord’s Test against England. Sulaiman and Kasim Khan also raised serious concerns about their father's health and conditions in prison, claiming that Pakistan authorities are trying to silence him.The controversy began during the second Test at Lord’s after Sky Sports aired an interview conducted by former England captain Michael Atherton with Sulaiman and Kasim.They spoke about their father's health and his conditions in prison.Reports later claimed that the PCB threatened not to send the Pakistan team out for the post-lunch session on the first day unless the interview was taken off air.‘They're clearly hoping to kill him in there’With Mohsin Naqvi facing increased scrutiny, the sons also spoke about their concerns over Khan's solitary confinement.Kasim made a serious allegation about the former Pakistan captain's safety.“They're clearly hoping to kill him in there. They want to silence him as secretly as possible and just slowly make him fade into nothing.“That's a very difficult thing to do with the most popular person in Pakistan right now. Their strategy, whenever we speak, is to let everything fizzle out and then impose more brutal restrictions that make it even harder for him to survive.”‘They made absolute fools of themselves’Kasim criticised the PCB's reported reaction and said the board had damaged its own image.“They made absolute fools of themselves,” Kasim told The Telegraph on Sunday.Sulaiman said he was surprised that the PCB reacted so strongly to an interview about his father.“I was expecting some sort of response. But I didn't think they would be so tactless as to threaten not to take to the field.“It shouldn't be in the remit of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to ask for an interview about an ex-Pakistan player, somebody who lived in England for 22 years, to be taken down. This wasn't about politics, but about the humanitarian situation and his health.”Authorities deny mistreatment claimsPakistani authorities have repeatedly denied allegations of mistreatment and have maintained that Khan is receiving proper medical care.Sulaiman, however, questioned those assurances and said the family had not been given enough information about his father's condition.“The worrying theory we're hearing is that they're drip-feeding these reports of his ailing health and pretending that they're trying to help him, just to lay the ground for something worse to happen. Then they can wash their hands and say: 'He's just an old man who died, and we had nothing to do with it.’“They haven't given us proof of any of this. It's all just hearsay from government sources – there's no transparency, they don't want to give anyone access, so how are we supposed to believe any of it? The last verifiable piece of information we had was from him, six months ago, when he spoke about his eye and how it had been neglected.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'If your idol backs you, you don't need anything more': Rajat Patidar on Virat Kohli's support
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Royal Challengers Bengaluru captain Rajat Patidar has revealed how Virat Kohli’s support helped him take on the captaincy of the IPL franch.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Royal Challengers Bengaluru captain Rajat Patidar has revealed how Virat Kohli’s support helped him take on the captaincy of the IPL franchise. Patidar said Kohli, whom he has admired for years, backed him strongly when he was given the responsibility of leading RCB.According to Patidar, having the support of his idol gave him confidence to handle the pressure of the role.‘If your idol backs you’Patidar spoke about Kohli’s influence and the special feeling of getting support from a player he had looked up to for a long time.“If your idol backs you, then you don’t need anything more. You don’t need anyone else’s support. I used to notice everything about him when he batted. From what he did on the ground to what his routine was off the field. Later, I came to know he backed me a lot, including when it came to captaincy,” Patidar told Sports Launchpad.Patidar said leading RCB is not an easy job because of the huge fan base and the expectations around the team.“It is not easy to hand someone the RCB captaincy, considering the fans and the expectations. He must have seen something in me. I don’t know what, but I have received a lot of support from him in the team, as a player and as a captain. He always backed me,” Patidar said.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.Patidar delivers for RCBPatidar quickly showed why the franchise trusted him with the captaincy.Under his leadership, RCB won their first IPL title in 2025, ending an 18-year wait for the trophy.The team then defended the title in 2026. Patidar became only the third captain to win consecutive IPL titles, joining MS Dhoni and Rohit Sharma.For Patidar, Kohli’s support has remained an important part of his leadership journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Pakistan cricket on a ventilator': Shoaib Akhtar’s brutal verdict as 'nothing' is expected from squad
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan cricket appears to be entering a major rebuilding phase after a disastrous start to the England tour, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) a.
articles.body: Pakistan cricket appears to be entering a major rebuilding phase after a disastrous start to the England tour, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) already making significant changes before the three-Test series has even reached its conclusion.England have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead after registering two emphatic victories. The hosts won the first Test at Headingley by an innings and 103 runs before securing a 194-run triumph at Lord’s. Pakistan’s poor performances have since triggered a major overhaul of the national setup.Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul have departed the coaching setup, while Mike Hesson has taken charge of the team with former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke joining him as an assistant.The PCB has also made a significant call on the playing group, removing seven players from the squad for the third and final Test. Among those sent back are senior names such as Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, with the board seemingly turning its attention towards a younger generation.Shoaib Akhtar explains PCB's thinkingFormer Pakistan fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar has now offered his assessment of the dramatic changes, claiming the PCB has effectively lost confidence in a large part of the existing squad.Speaking on the OutSide EDGE show, Akhtar suggested that the board is no longer simply reacting to the England defeats but is instead using the tour as an opportunity to accelerate a wider rebuilding process.“The PCB itself was very disappointed by these people, and they don’t expect anything from this Pakistan squad. The plan is to remove this squad and replace them with younger and newer blood. Players who just want to play for Pakistan. They are looking at the future now, and they are working at it in the right way,” Akhtar said.The former pacer, however, stressed that Pakistan must be careful while making such a transition. He specifically named Shaheen Shah Afridi, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf as three players whose careers should be protected as the team undergoes major changes.“In this transition, I just want Shaheen Shah Afridi, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf’s careers to be saved. These guys have a lot of cricket left in them,” he said.'Nothing' expected from current Pakistan squadAkhtar also claimed that a conversation with a PCB official gave him a revealing insight into the board's expectations from the current team.According to the former Pakistan pacer, he asked the official what the PCB expected from the side during its England tour. The response, he said, was blunt.“Nothing. We have expectations from the next generation of players that we are preparing for the big stage,” Akhtar quoted the official as saying.Akhtar further claimed that the same official described the state of Pakistan cricket as being “on a ventilator” and believed it could take around two years to revive the national setup.The comments underline the scale of the challenge facing the PCB, particularly after Pakistan's inability to put up a strong fight in either of the first two Tests.Akhtar questions Pakistan's lack of fightThe 51-year-old also spoke about what he saw during his visit to the National Cricket Academy in Lahore. Akhtar said he was there during the second Test and noticed considerable infrastructure work taking place.“After 26 years, there is work being done at the academy now,” Akhtar said.Despite the upheaval surrounding the senior team, Akhtar suggested that the developments should not have come as a surprise.When asked whether the turmoil had shocked him, he responded: “What is the shock there? Didn’t you expect that?”He was equally critical when Pakistan's struggles against England were discussed. Reflecting on the two heavy defeats, Akhtar summed up the team's performances in stark terms.“We didn’t have the fight in us,” he said.Pakistan will now travel to Edgbaston for the third Test, where they will attempt to prevent England from completing a 3-0 series whitewash. However, the decisions taken by the PCB before the series has even ended suggest that the problems confronting Pakistan cricket are being viewed as much bigger than the outcome of this England tour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Cosmetic surgery’ won’t fix Pakistan cricket: Misbah-ul-Haq takes aim at PCB after stepping down
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Pakistan Test captain Misbah-ul-Haq has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) for what he described as a reactive approach to handling th.
articles.body: Former Pakistan Test captain Misbah-ul-Haq has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) for what he described as a reactive approach to handling the national team, following the decision to send seven players and two coaches back home during the ongoing Test tour of England.Misbah, who recently resigned as Pakistan’s national selector, stepped down shortly after the PCB announced its decision earlier this week. The development came after the board issued show-cause notices to every member of the selection committee.The PCB’s decision saw head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul released from the Test squad, while seven players were also removed. Pakistan subsequently sent its white-ball players to England for the final match of the series.Misbah alleges double standardsSpeaking on a television show, Misbah questioned the way local coaches are treated compared with their foreign counterparts in Pakistan cricket.According to the former captain, overseas coaches are given greater authority while facing considerably less scrutiny when results do not go their way."It is a fact that local and foreign coaches are treated differently in Pakistan cricket. Local coaches have to face more scrutiny and criticism when compared to foreign coaches," he said.Misbah made it clear that his criticism was not directed at the appointment of overseas coaches themselves. Instead, he argued that the wider cricketing ecosystem tends to give foreign coaches an easier ride."I don't think there is anything wrong in having foreign coaches but what bothers me is we (fans, critics, media, PCB) tend to have a soft corner for foreign coaches," he added.He further explained that the imbalance extends to the level of responsibility placed on coaches."We tend to give foreign coaches more authority and power and he is held less responsible if the team performs poorly. In contrast, local coaches always facing scrutiny from everyone."'We shouldn't panic'Misbah also took aim at the PCB’s decision-making process, warning that sudden changes made under pressure could create more problems for a team already in need of stability.He argued that Pakistan cannot afford to repeatedly overhaul its setup without first conducting a proper assessment of performances and identifying the reasons behind its struggles."We shouldn't panic and do cosmetic surgery because of pressure. We need to analyse performances and the situation and then decide how to move forward," Misbah said.The former selector added: "Unfortunately, we are used to taking reactive decisions in Pakistan cricket."For Misbah, the solution requires patience and a long-term strategy rather than immediate responses to poor results.Misbah points to India's modelThe former Pakistan captain also compared the country's cricketing structure with India's, highlighting the gradual development of the Indian system since the 1990s.He pointed to Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli as examples from the Indian setup and argued that India's success against Pakistan has been helped by greater exposure and stronger preparation for pressure situations."Our youngsters are playing too much white-ball cricket and their exposure to red-ball cricket is limited. Not enough four-day cricket. This means they have more chances of cracking under pressure."India took time to process and develop and they made gradual investments in their system after the 90s. There is no quick fix to the system."Misbah's comments come at a turbulent time for Pakistan cricket, with the PCB making major changes to the Test setup even before the England tour has concluded. His message, however, was that lasting improvement will require consistency, greater red-ball exposure for young players and sustained investment rather than repeated reactions to short-term setbacks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia announce squad for South Africa Tests: Marnus Labuschagne survives, Cooper Connolly earns surprise inclusion
articles.summary: Cricket News: Marnus Labuschagne has survived another selection scare, with Cricket Australia retaining the struggling batter in its 16-member Test squad for the up.
articles.body: Marnus Labuschagne has survived another selection scare, with Cricket Australia retaining the struggling batter in its 16-member Test squad for the upcoming three-match series against South Africa.The decision came despite growing calls for Labuschagne to be dropped. Australia greats Ricky Ponting and Matthew Hayden have both questioned his place in the side, but chief selector George Bailey has opted to continue backing the right-hander.Labuschagne's recent record has done little to strengthen his case. It has been more than three years since he last scored a Test century, with his most recent hundred coming in July 2023. Across his last 43 Test innings, he has averaged just 24.69.His struggles have already cost him his place in Australia's ODI squad for the series against South Africa. However, the selectors have continued to show faith in him in the longer format.That backing comes despite Labuschagne managing scores of only 1, 31 and 4 across his three innings against Bangladesh.Australia add three players to Test squadThe upcoming series will be the first meeting between Australia and South Africa since last year's World Test Championship Final at Lord's. The results in this series could have a major bearing on which teams eventually qualify for next year's WTC decider at The Oval.Alongside Labuschagne, the selectors have retained 13 players from the squad that featured in Australia's most recent Test against Bangladesh in Mackay, which Pat Cummins' side won inside two days.Cooper Connolly, Michael Neser and Matthew Kuhnemann are the three additions to the 16-man group.Connolly's inclusion is notable given his limited experience in first-class cricket. The left-hander is yet to score a first-class century and has batted at No.3 only once. He was also recently dropped by Western Australia for their final Sheffield Shield match last summer.Neser, meanwhile, returns after recovering from a calf strain sustained during a training camp in early August. His inclusion gives Australia five fast-bowling options, with Neser joining captain Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Scott Boland.Cameron Green and Beau Webster are the two all-rounders included in the squad and are expected to feature in Australia's playing XI for the opening Test in Durban.Matt Renshaw has also retained his place as an opener. The left-hander had previously come into the squad in place of Jake Weatherald after Weatherald struggled in the first Test against Bangladesh.Explaining the selection, Bailey highlighted the demands of the South Africa tour, with the Test series coming after six ODIs and featuring short gaps between matches."This is a reasonably condensed three-game series, on the back of six one-day internationals, with only short breaks between each game. The squad provides balance and options for each Test and the variety of conditions we may face,” Chair of Selectors George Bailey said in an official statement.The three-Test series will begin in Durban on October 9, before moving to Gqeberha and Cape Town.The tour marks Australia's first Test trip to South Africa since the infamous 2018 series, when the sandpaper gate scandal rocked the team.Only five members of the current touring party have previously been part of an Australian squad that travelled to South Africa for a Test series: Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Steve Smith and Matt Renshaw.Australia Test squad for tour of South Africa: Pat Cummins (captain), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Matthew Kuhnemann, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Michael Neser, Matthew Renshaw, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, Beau Webster.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Duleep Trophy final: Ishan Kishan fires after Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s cameo, puts East on solid footing
articles.summary: Cricket News: CHENNAI: There was a good Sunday crowd at the MA Chidambaram Stadium to watch teen sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi fire. They got a glimpse of it, but .
articles.body: CHENNAI: There was a good Sunday crowd at the MA Chidambaram Stadium to watch teen sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi fire. They got a glimpse of it, but it was Ishan Kishan who stole the show on the opening day of the Duleep Trophy final here on Sunday.After Sooryavanshi enthralled in the first hour with a breezy 37-ball 44 taking apart Mohammed Siraj, Kishan, batting at No. 5, struck his 10th firstclass century, remaining unbeaten on 111 off 135 balls (14x4, 1x6), to put his side firmly in command against South Zone. Kishan, who is currently out of India’s red-ball set-up, made the most of the easy batting conditions and tiring South attack on a hot day as East Zone closed at 385-4 in 79 overs.Kishan, who reached his half-century off 71 balls, accelerated after reaching the milestone, bringing up his second fifty in just 51 balls. He completed his century off 122 balls, driving veteran leggie Shreyas Gopal, playing his 100th First-Class match, straight down the ground for a boundary.He was given excellent support by right-hander Kumar Kushagra, who is unbeaten on 63 off 75 balls (4x4, 5x6). The pair stitched an unbeaten 144-run fifth-wicket partnership, leaving East Zone in a commanding position.Earlier, after Kishan won the toss and opted to bat, all eyes were on Sooryavanshi. The teenager did not take long to entertain, smashing two boundaries off MD Nidhees in the sixth over, one off the front foot and another off the back foot, both through the cover region.He then took on Siraj, hitting the pacer for a boundary and a six over long-off before dispatching the final ball of the over for another four. With East Zone racing to 50 in just 7.5 overs, South skipper Tilak Varma was forced to introduce off-spinner Tripurana Vijay, who extracted sharp turn with his first delivery.South employed a defensive field for the 15-year-old, with five fielders stationed outside the ring on the leg and off sides, which is unusual so early in a five-day game.Siraj endured an expensive opening spell, conceding 41 runs in five overs. East Zone reached 70-0 in 10 overs and then 100 in 14.3 overs. Abhimanyu Easwaran (72 off 86 balls) matched Sooryavanshi’s aggression and brought up his 50 in 46 balls.However, the opening stand was broken at 100 when Chama Milind (2-56) dismissed Sooryavanshi for 44 off 37 balls. The youngster attempted to pull a short delivery but mistimed it, with substitute Tanay Thyagarajan completing the catch running in from deep square leg. Easwaran looked extremely assured and seemed set for a century, but was run out.BRIEF SCORES: East Zone 385-4 (Easwaran 72, Mohan 85, Kishan 111*, Kushagra 63*; C Milind 2-56) vs South.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Gen Next sets the pace: Four young women fast bowlers eye India selection after 13,000-strong talent hunt
articles.summary: Cricket News: BENGALURU: Sometimes, all it takes to unlock talent is a spark. It can come from within or from someone willing to light it for you. For Akshita Bhaga.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Sometimes, all it takes to unlock talent is a spark. It can come from within or from someone willing to light it for you. For Akshita Bhagat, Palak Singh, Rohita Chowdry and Joshna Angel, the WPL Speed Queen initiative provided that spark.The four were among more than 13,000 aspirants who registered for the talent hunt. Around 7,500 made it to the trials before 56 finalists showcased their speed, strength and ambition at the finale in Mumbai earlier this year. Their performances have since opened another door.Having earned the opportunity to train under some of the best coaches and observe some of the finest cricketers at the BCCI Centre of Excellence, the four fast bowlers are now aiming higher. They are currently training under coach Krishna Kumar at CoE. TOI takes a look at the future India prospects...AKSHITA BHAGATThe first to make the big leap is Mohali teenager Akshita. The 19-year old was last month named in the India ‘A’ one-day squad for the upcoming home series against Australia ‘A’, a significant step in a journey that began with gully cricket.Akshita joined has represented Punjab in national age-group and senior domestic tournaments. She started out as a batter before switching to pace bowling and counts India captain Harmanpreet Kaur among her role models. For her, Speed Queen provided the exposure and belief to accelerate that journey.“There were a lot of learnings from the Speed Queen and the camp here has furthered that. The coaches worked on our tactics and basics. I learned what I can improve, what I need to work on and, more importantly, learnt the importance of hard work. Also, being around established players has allowed me to pick their brains,” said Akshita, a huge fan of former South African pacer Dale Steyn and Australian great Ellyse Perry.With a senior India camp now in her sights, Akshita feels the CoE experience has been defining. “I didn’t expect to come to the CoE so soon, where you get the best strength and conditioning facilities and coaches. When I started, the dream was to play for India, but I didn’t think I would take such a huge step towards it so soon,” she said.JOSHNA ANGELAt 15, Joshna is a pocket dynamo — petite and bubbly off the field, fierce and fast with a ball in hand. The Chennai teenager clocked 108 kmph during the trials. Her introduction to both the sport and bowling came from her father, R Jesuraj, a former Tamil Nadu medium pacer.Joshna took up cricket out of boredom during the Covid-19 lockdown. She is now dreaming big. “The Speed Queen program helped me gain confidence and get to know my strengths,” said Joshna, who has represented Tamil Nadu in the U-15 and U-19 categories.Her father remains one of her inspirations, along with England pacer Lauren Bell. The CoE camp, meanwhile, has opened her eyes to the demands of elite sport. “One of the key lessons has been how to stay focused and be sincere in maintaining the diet. There has also been a lot of emphasis on exercising, which has taught me a lot,” she said.Meeting India internationals Tilak Varma and Sanju Samson has been another highlight. As for the ultimate goal, there was no hesitation. “I want to play for India,” she declared boldly.PALAK SINGHAthletics was Palak’s first calling. Cricket, however, was the sport her father chose for her. Three years after taking up the game, the 15-year old has already shown that she can generate serious pace. She clocked 108 kmph in the zonal trials and 106 kmph in the finale. Inspired by Australian fast bowler Mitchell Starc, Palak is now learning to make the most of her height while understanding that pace is only one part of the equation.“Coming here is a big thing. It’s a very good opportunity and a valuable experience to train under some of the best coaches in the country. I have understood my bowling better, and I now know that a bowler should also have accuracy, consistency, swing and variations,” she said.Having cut her teeth in the state age group team, Palak now has a more immediate target: breaking into the India U-19 side. “From here, I will get a good pathway to play for India in the future. I am only 15, so I have the India U-19 team to look ahead to,” she said.ROHITA CHOWDRYRohita’s journey to pace bowling began on the track. A former heptathlete, the Bengaluru youngster took up cricket at her father’s insistence. Given her athleticism and natural speed, fast bowling was an obvious fit.The 24-year old has represented various Karnataka teams but was going through a difficult phase before the Speed Queen opportunity came her way. “I was going struggling to make my place in the senior Karnataka team. I was hesitant to even participate in the event. But because of it, I regained a lot of confidence; it came as a ray of hope,” said Rohita, who clocked 109 kmph in the initial round before touching 104 kmph in the finale.The CoE experience has since given that confidence another boost. “This is what dreams are made of. Bumping into international cricketers and learning from their process has been crucial. I’ve learnt that there is so much more to just bowling fast. There’s so much that goes into our nutrition, fitness training and running programmes,” she said.Rohita, who holds a degree in international relations, public policy and journalism, always had the backing of her parents. She draws inspiration from Jhulan Goswami’s longevity and says a conversation with CoE head of cricket VVS Laxman has been one of the highlights of the camp.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Scared to work’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer opens up on Mohsin Naqvi-led PCB
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to overhaul the national team in the middle of its England tour continues to face scrutiny, with former Pakistan.
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to overhaul the national team in the middle of its England tour continues to face scrutiny, with former Pakistan spinner Mushtaq Ahmed admitting that the uncertainty surrounding coaching positions has made him wary of taking up a role with the national side.A week after the PCB sent seven players and two coaches back to Pakistan, the fallout from the decision remains a major talking point. The board has frequently faced criticism for making repeated changes to its coaches and captains, and Mushtaq believes that the lack of stability is now becoming a deterrent for former players who want to serve Pakistan in coaching roles.The PCB took the drastic step after Pakistan suffered heavy defeats in the opening two Tests against England. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha were among the players sent home, while Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were also removed from the coaching setup. They were replaced in the dressing room by Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke.Mushtaq reveals why he is hesitantMushtaq was asked whether he would be interested in coaching Pakistan and made it clear that he would welcome the chance to work with the national team. However, he also explained why the current environment leaves him concerned about accepting such a responsibility.The former spinner pointed to the treatment of coaches and the possibility of being removed abruptly, even while a tour is still in progress.“I would love to do that for my country, of course. Especially at this time. Obviously, I need only one thing. Sometimes you get scared of working for your own country when the people don’t respect you, and they sack you because of a few emotional decisions here and there. When you see those things, people getting sacked on a tour, you get worried and scared,” Mushtaq said on the BBC Stumped Podcast.Despite his concerns, Mushtaq believes there is an opportunity for Pakistani coaches to make a meaningful contribution if greater stability can be established within the system.“I think those are the things that if you can get that sorted, I think every Pakistani cricketer who is coaching, not only myself, they’d love to serve the country. This is the best time for me to take that challenge and bring those players to their best, make them confident about international cricket and make a unit that can actually challenge opposition teams,” he added.'This is not the right thing'Mushtaq also strongly disagreed with the PCB's decision to make such sweeping changes while the England series was still underway.The former Pakistan international, who played 52 Tests and 144 ODIs, questioned the rationale behind sending seven players home and altering the coaching staff midway through an overseas tour.“Changing seven players and the management, especially with the tour still going on, I feel that this is not the right thing,” Mushtaq said.He was particularly critical of the timing of the decision involving Sarfaraz and Umar Gul, arguing that changes of this magnitude should have been considered after the completion of the tour.“This has never happened in Pakistan cricket before. Obviously, I’m hurt as an ex-cricketer, as a Pakistani, these things should not happen. Sarfaraz and Umar Gul, they are some of the most experienced cricketers. They serve the country very well. Sarfaraz was a captain also. If you want to sack them, obviously, you have to sack them after the tour. This is the time to stay calm, don’t make rash decisions," he added.PCB under growing scrutinyThe mid-tour shake-up has attracted criticism beyond Pakistan, with Michael Atherton, Nasser Hussain and Jason Gillespie among those who have questioned the PCB's decision.The board's changes came after Pakistan's disappointing results in the first two Tests, leaving the team facing the prospect of a difficult end to the tour.Pakistan will now look to finish the series on a positive note when they face England in the third and final Test, beginning on September 9 in Birmingham. However, with questions over the board's approach to coaches, players and decision-making continuing to mount, the debate surrounding Pakistan cricket is unlikely to end with the conclusion of the Test series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Govt crossing line in RCA politics: Ashok Gehlot
articles.summary: Cricket News: JAIPUR: Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot launched a scathing attack on the BJP govt, raising severe concerns over political interference i.
articles.body: JAIPUR: Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot launched a scathing attack on the BJP govt, raising severe concerns over political interference in the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) and accusing the state administration of derailing major infrastructure projects, including the international stadium at Chonp.Expressing anguish over the persistent administrative crisis in the state’s cricket body, Gehlot lamented the lack of international cricket action in the capital. “Unfortunately, for the past five years, no international matches are being hosted here anymore. This should be a matter of concern,” the veteran Congress leader said, taking aim at the govt over the prolonged governance vacuum.It was in Nov 2021, under the tenure of his son Vaibhav Gehlot as RCA president, that the Sawai Man Singh Stadium last hosted an international fixture — a T20I between India and New Zealand.Speaking as the chief guest at the 33rd Mathura Das Mathur Awards on Sunday, Gehlot felicitated upcoming state cricketers across sub-junior, junior and senior categories.His remarks come against the backdrop of unprecedented turmoil within the RCA. The association has been managed by govt-appointed ad hoc committees, which have seen intense internal power struggles, factional rivalries and failure to conduct democratic elections.Hitting out at the BJP dispensation for crossing limits in sports administration, Gehlot added, “The politics going on in cricket is very painful. Rajasthan’s history is deeply linked with cricket. Politics happens everywhere nowadays; it even happens in the judiciary. It happens everywhere, in every field. It happens in sports associations as well. But it should not be to the extent that sports and sports associations suffer. Such politics, I believe, should not happen. A line should not be crossed. Now, the govt itself is crossing that line.”Gehlot particularly targeted the delay in holding RCA elections. “It has been three years for this govt, and so far, there is no news about RCA elections. Ad hoc panels have been formed. Such a situation existing at the government level is, I believe, painful,” he remarked, urging chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma to respect the youth’s passion for cricket and facilitate immediate elections.Comparing his tenure’s initiatives, such as the creation of the Barkatullah Khan Stadium in Jodhpur, 2% sports reservation in govt jobs, and the Rural/Urban Olympics, with the current administration, Gehlot asserted that the BJP govt has failed on sports commitments.He highlighted the stalled progress of the world-class Chonp Stadium, envisioned during Vaibhav’s tenure as RCA president in collaboration with industrialist Anil Agarwal. “When CP Joshi and Vaibhav were there, we had a talk with Anil Agarwal... He promised to give Rs 250 to Rs 300 crore. I heard he even gave Rs 100 to Rs 150 crore,” Gehlot noted, calling on the state govt to engage with Vedant Group’s chairperson to resume the construction of the facility.Gehlot concluded that key public infrastructure across the state, from cricket stadiums to the FinTech Institute and IPD Tower, has faced unnecessary delays under the current regime, calling for immediate corrective action in public interest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Trophy controversy returns? Mohsin Naqvi set to attend India’s Women’s Asia Cup final
articles.summary: Cricket News: The possibility of another trophy presentation controversy involving India and Pakistan has emerged ahead of the ACC Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final, with.
articles.body: The possibility of another trophy presentation controversy involving India and Pakistan has emerged ahead of the ACC Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final, with Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman and Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi set to attend the summit clash in Dubai.According to a Geo Super report, Naqvi is expected to be the chief guest at the closing ceremony of the tournament on September 13. His presence could once again bring the focus on the trophy presentation if Harmanpreet Kaur’s India reach the final and go on to win the title.Naqvi was at the centre of a major controversy during last year's Men's Asia Cup final at the Dubai International Stadium. India defeated Pakistan in the summit clash but refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi, who was the ACC president and also PCB chairman.The episode took place against a particularly tense backdrop. The Men's Asia Cup was played after the Pahalgam terror attack, while Naqvi had also shared anti-India statements on social media during the tournament in his capacity as Pakistan's Interior Minister.Trophy drama could returnWith Naqvi expected to attend the Women's Asia Cup final, another trophy-related standoff could potentially unfold.If India win the tournament, Naqvi could be the official presenting the silverware to the champions because of his position as ACC president. The decision on whether to accept it from him, however, would ultimately rest with the Harmanpreet-led Indian team.The BCCI has so far remained silent on what the women's side would do if they win the tournament and Naqvi is present for the presentation.India are among the favourites for the title and have already secured their place in the semi-finals without losing a match. They made a particularly strong statement against Pakistan, defeating the Fatima Sana-led side by seven wickets after bowling them out for just 55 in Dubai.What happened in last year's final?The controversy involving Naqvi began after India defeated Pakistan in the Men's Asia Cup final on September 28, 2025.The Suryakumar Yadav-led Indian side completed the victory, but the post-match presentation was delayed by more than an hour as discussions continued over who would present the trophy.India eventually chose not to receive the silverware from Naqvi. The players celebrated their title triumph on the podium without the trophy, while Naqvi left the stadium with it.The Asia Cup trophy has still not been handed over to India and remains at the ACC office in Dubai.The situation became one of the most talked-about moments of the tournament, particularly because Naqvi had attended the final despite the earlier tensions between the two sides.Why would Naqvi present the trophy?Naqvi holds two key positions relevant to the presentation. He is the PCB chairman as well as the president of the ACC.Since the Women's Asia Cup is an ACC-hosted tournament, Naqvi, by virtue of his position as ACC president, holds the right to present the trophy to the winners.That means another India-Pakistan trophy moment could be waiting in Dubai if Harmanpreet Kaur's team reaches the final and lifts the title.India dominate Women's Asia Cup campaignIndia have been unbeaten throughout their campaign in the eight-team Women's Asia Cup. Harmanpreet Kaur's side began the tournament with a victory over Thailand before producing convincing wins against Hong Kong and Pakistan in the group stage.The tournament has also witnessed a major individual milestone for Smriti Mandhana, who became the leading run-scorer in women's international cricket after surpassing former India captain Mithali Raj.With India already through to the semi-finals, attention will now turn to the knockout stage. If the Women in Blue make it all the way to the final and win the trophy on September 13, Naqvi's presence could set the stage for another closely watched presentation ceremony in Dubai.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
